@marco I’m pissed about Desert Palms. You told me Saturday all 14 units were done, but not one code made it into the sheet. Yvette called this morning because the tenant in 9B lost her key and needs three copies today. Now we’ve got nothing to cut them from.

This is the second time I’ve had to get on you about this. I told you in September to put the Kessler codes in the sheet. Before that, I told everybody in August: every rekey and every master job gets the address, unit and bitting code in the sheet the same day, before you leave the van. No exceptions. That wasn’t a suggestion.

Go back to Desert Palms today. Decode 9B first so we can get Yvette those three keys today. Then decode the other units too if you can, all 14 if possible, and get the address, unit numbers and codes into the sheet. Let me know when 9B is done and what you were able to get on the rest. If you can’t get all of them today, tell me what’s left and why.

Yvette also found a black pinning tray with pins in it on the leasing office counter. Pick up my tray while you’re there and bring it back to the shop.

You’re good with your hands, Marco, and I know you can do the work. But the job isn’t finished when the locks are done. The paperwork and our tools are part of it too. I should not have to chase you down for this again.
